title: The constant periodic resolution and its nonzero quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $t\in R$ satisfy $t^2=0$ and $\{r\in R:tr=0\}=tR$, and put $F=R/tR$. Let $V$ be any scheme, with its small pro-etale site and size convention [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $R_V,F_V$ for the constant ring and module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], with the $R_V$-action on $F_V$ induced by the quotient $R\to F$. Define $P_V$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] by $P_V^i=R_V$ for $i\leq0$, $P_V^i=0$ for $i>0$, and differential multiplication by the constant section $t$ for $i<0$, zero otherwise. Let $\pi_V:P_V^0\to F_V$ be the constant quotient map. Then $\cdots\xrightarrow{t}R_V\xrightarrow{t}R_V\xrightarrow{\pi_V}F_V\to0$ is exact, and the map $P_V\to F_V[0]$ with degree-zero component $\pi_V$ is a K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex]. More precisely, the kernel and the image of multiplication by $t$ on $R_V$ coincide, its cokernel is canonically $F_V$, all terms of $P_V$ are flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and multiplication by $t$ on $F_V$ is zero. If $V$ is nonempty, the canonical map from $F$ to the underlying abelian group $F_V(V)$, taking an element to its constant section, is injective. Consequently $F\ne0$ and nonempty $V$ imply $F_V\ne0$. No nonvanishing is claimed for empty $V$, and no finiteness or connectedness condition is imposed.

proof.text: Let $\mu:R\to R$ send $r$ to $tr$, and let $q:R\to F$ be the quotient. Its image is $tR$, its kernel is $tR$ by hypothesis, and $q$ is surjective with kernel $tR$. Thus $\ker\mu=\operatorname{im}\mu$ and $\operatorname{coker}\mu=F$ via $q$. Also $\mu^2(r)=t^2r=0$ and $t\bar r=\overline{tr}=0$ in $F$. These calculations include the zero ring.

proof.text: Work in the fixed pro-etale site and lift coefficients to the prescribed common universe. Constant module presheaves preserve limits and colimits objectwise, by joint reflection through the evaluation functors. Module sheafification preserves finite limits and colimits, as does coefficient transport along the canonical isomorphism from the constant ring sheafification to the underlying constant commutative ring sheaf. Thus the sized constant module functor is exact and additive. Its rank-one object is isomorphic to the unit module: extend the ring sheafification unit using the module sheafification universal property, and prove this extension is an isomorphism from local bijectivity of both additive and ring sheafification units. Transport the algebraic exact sequences from step 1. Exactness and surjectivity identify the cokernel canonically with the constant quotient. The scalar endomorphism acts by a restriction-compatible global section of the constant ring sheaf, via the unit-module Hom equivalence. Its square is zero by the algebraic calculation and functoriality. Multiplication by t on the quotient maps to zero by additivity.

Conjugate the transported scalar map C(mu) by the canonical rank-one isomorphism to obtain an endomorphism f of the unit module over the constant commutative ring sheaf. The unit-module Hom equivalence gives a restriction-compatible section s with multiplication map f. Linearity and f squared equal to zero give s_U squared equal to zero on every object U. Transported algebraic exactness gives kernel(f) equal to image(f). Apply [lem-sfb-exact-scalar-periodic-resolution] to s. Compose each nonpositive term identification with the inverse rank-one isomorphism: the differential equation follows by conjugation and the periodic-complex term equations; all positive terms are zero and all terms are flat. The cokernel isomorphism induced by rank-one conjugation, followed by step 2's cokernel isomorphism, identifies the augmentation target with the prescribed constant quotient. Postcompose the augmentation by the induced isomorphism of single complexes. Its degree-zero component is the constant quotient map by the cokernel equations, all other components are zero, and this postcomposition preserves quasi-isomorphism and the K-flat source.

proof.text: Assume V is nonempty and two elements of F give equal constant sections. Apply Mathlib's local injectivity of the additive sheafification unit to obtain a covering equalizer sieve. The bottom sieve cannot cover the terminal pro-etale object V: a covering family is jointly surjective and a chosen point of V must lift to some member. Restrictions in the constant module presheaf are identities, so if the original constants differed their equalizer sieve would be bottom. This contradiction proves their equality, after removing the injective coefficient-universe lift.
